**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), paragraph p0063 (Section 10.3).**

What I found:

- **Section 10.3 "Assignment"** is not an assignment clause at all — it is a successors-and-assigns / no-third-party-beneficiary statement. It contains no consent mechanics in either direction.
- **Good news on our side:** there is no prohibition on Company assignment, and no change-of-control language anywhere in the agreement (a search for "change of control" returns nothing). The only termination rights are the mutual 90-day convenience right (p0024) and our own 70-day right (p0011) — neither is triggered by our change of control. So the walk-away scenarios (blanket bar on our assignment; vendor termination or re-pricing on our CoC) are absent.
- **Why it still fails the fallback:** the clause gives us no control over HDI. HDI is free to transfer the entire site development and hosting relationship — including access to our confidential merchandising and customer data under Sections 9 — to any transferee, including a competitor, with no notice and no consent. The fallback requires at minimum consent for non-successor assignments, not to be unreasonably withheld.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) adds one sentence pair to 10.3: an express affiliate/successor carve-out for us plus confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination, suspension or re-pricing right, and a consent (not unreasonably withheld) plus no-competitor gate on HDI's assignment. The comment offers the mutual notice-based fallback if HDI pushes back.
